title: refuses a version with no section, naming the heading to add
why: A tag whose version has no section answered with an empty one: a Release drafted with nothing under What changed, and no prompt to write it.

title: refuses a final with no Security or an empty one, and takes "None."
why: The final-needs-Security rule dropped: a release's notes can stay silent on whether it fixes a vulnerability, which release_notes_vulns asks them to say.

title: refuses a final whose section is not dated, and a heading in neither form
why: A final release drafted from a section that does not say when it was released, so the changelog never records the day.

title: reads a candidate's section, dated or not, up to the next version or the links
why: The last section runs on into the link references at the foot, so the oldest release's notes would end with the changelog's own link list.

title: fill What changed and Known issues from the tag's section, under their headings
why: Known issues left among the changes: the notes say them twice, once under What changed.

title: carry a final's Security, and say none is fixed where it says None.
why: A bare "None." under Security in a release's notes, not the sentence that says no publicly known vulnerability is fixed.

title: refuse a section that names no change, or says nothing of its known issues
why: A section with no Known issues fills the notes' heading with nothing, which reads as a claim that there are none.

title: make the changelog's relative links absolute, at the tag
why: The changelog's links to docs/install.md and SUPPORT.md copied as they are, which lead nowhere from the Releases page.

title: name the changelog's three keys once each, under their headings and before the downloads
why: The template's Known issues heading with nothing under it: fillNotes cannot refuse a key the template no longer names.

title: finds package.json's version in the committed changelog, ready for its next candidate
why: The committed changelog with no section for package.json's version: the next candidate's tag would draft nothing, found only on the tag's run.

title: from the command line, write the filled notes to the file named
why: The notes command reading a changelog that is not the committed one: every tag's notes refused, seen only when a tag's release job fails.
